12882742_62b60170.text: The intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) is a flat retinorecipient thalamic structure implicated in orchestrating circadian rhythm, historically considered to be a subdivision of the neighboring ventrolateral geniculate nucleus (VLG). IGL consists of two main neuronal subpopulations: enkephalinergic and neuropeptide Y (NPY)-synthesizing cells. These cell types have different functions, connectivity and firing pattern in vivo, which suggest that they have different membrane currents to support their functional differences
12882742_62b60170.section: Anatomical location and structural organization of IGL neurons

12882742_30978228.text: .Our results suggest that IGL neurons can be divided into two subpopulations based on two ionic currents. A T-type calcium current (IT) was identified in neurons that do not synthesise NPY, whereas all NPY-positive neurons were found to express a marked A-type potassium current (IA).
